intent: The top-level per-node server object: owns the sync thread and worker thread pool, the command queues, the listening ports, the loaded plugins and DB pool, and the shutdown/detach state machine, implementing the SQLiteServer interface SQLiteNode uses to call back into it.

objects.name: BedrockServer
objects.role: The server: owns threads, queues, ports, plugins, and DB pool; implements SQLiteServer

objects.name: BedrockServer::SHUTDOWN_STATE
objects.role: The four states of the shutdown state machine (RUNNING/START_SHUTDOWN/COMMANDS_FINISHED/DONE)

objects.name: BedrockServer::BedrockServerUpgradeCommand
objects.role: Nested BedrockCommand that runs every plugin's DB schema upgrade once, the first time this node stands up as leader

objects.name: BedrockServer::syncWrapper/sync
objects.role: Sync thread body: brings up SQLiteNode/DB pool, starts workers, drives the poll/update loop, runs the upgrade command, drains shutdown

objects.name: BedrockServer::worker
objects.role: Worker thread body: dequeues from the main or blocking queue and calls runCommand in a loop

objects.name: BedrockServer::runCommand
objects.role: Core peek/process/commit/retry state machine for one command, including escalation and conflict-retry backoff

objects.name: BedrockServer::handleSocket
objects.role: Per-connection thread: polls a client socket, deserializes requests, runs each command on its own thread to watch for disconnect/abort

objects.name: BedrockServer::buildCommandFromRequest
objects.role: Builds a command from a raw request via the plugins, handling fire-and-forget and attached HTTPS sub-requests

objects.name: BedrockServer::_reply
objects.role: Sends a completed command's response back over its socket or via its owning plugin

objects.name: BedrockServer::_control/_isControlCommand/_isNonSecureControlCommand
objects.role: Implements the localhost-only control command surface (BeginBackup, SuppressCommandPort, ClearCrashCommands, ConflictReport, Detach/Attach, EnableSQLTracing, CRASH_COMMAND, ClearBlockingQueue, SetConflictParams/SetConflictPageLocks, SetBlockingQueueTimeRateLimit, BlockWrites/UnblockWrites, SetMaxSocketThreads, SetPriority, GetCommitHash)

objects.name: BedrockServer::_wouldCrash/_generateCrashMessage/onNodeLogin
objects.role: Tracks commands known to have crashed a node, refuses to rerun them, broadcasts the block list to peers

objects.name: BedrockServer::_beginShutdown/shutdownComplete/isShuttingDown
objects.role: Drives the shutdown/standdown state machine documented at length in the header

objects.name: BedrockServer::_acceptSockets
objects.role: Accepts pending connections on all open ports and spawns a handleSocket thread per connection

objects.name: shutdownTimer
objects.role: Four steady_clock timestamps logged once in the destructor to report shutdown-phase durations

objects.name: __quiesceLock/__quiesceShouldUnlock/__quiesceThread
objects.role: Hold the single outstanding exclusive-DB-lock thread used to implement BlockWrites/UnblockWrites

misfits.why: Plain (non-static) file-scope globals with external linkage rather than BedrockServer members, holding exactly the kind of per-server state (which thread owns the DB quiesce lock) this file otherwise keeps private; their double-leading-underscore names are also identifiers reserved to the implementation by the C++ standard

Public list<string> whose doc comment references an 'instance of commandPortSuppressionCount', a type that does not exist anywhere in the repo; the member itself is never read or written anywhere, a dead vestige of an earlier refactor of suppressCommandPort

One ~250-line function directly owns the tuning knobs of several otherwise-separate subsystems (conflict retry counts and page-lock policy, the blocking queue's rate-limit windows, DB quiesce, socket-thread caps, sync-node priority, journal hash lookup) instead of delegating each to its own subsystem

name_fit.note: BedrockServer.h/.cpp is exactly the server class it names

location_fit.note: Root-level orchestrator alongside its peers (BedrockCommand, BedrockPlugin), matching class_hierarchy.md's placement of BedrockServer as SQLiteServer's concrete subclass

naming_quality.note: Consistent `_` prefix on private members and honestly-labeled legacy aliases (isUpgradeComplete, suppressCommandPort), but the reserved double-underscore quiesce globals are a real violation
